title: How many vehicles carry all the children on the trip?
description: Joseph's school has girls and boys going on a trip. The video adds them and then shares them into equal groups for four kinds of vehicle.
teaching_notes: One idea: vehicles needed is the number of children shared into groups of the size one vehicle carries. Watch for children who think a bigger vehicle needs more vehicles.

video_script.why: The child must find how many vehicles carry a whole school, which means adding first and then sharing into equal groups.
video_script.substitution: Add the girls and boys to get the total, then divide the total by the number one vehicle carries.
video_script.anchor: Joseph's school trip with a line of vehicles outside the school gate in Kochi
video_script.wrong_answer: a big car is bigger, so it needs more vehicles
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu thinks a bigger vehicle needs more vehicles. A vehicle that carries more children means fewer vehicles are needed.
video_script.payoff_line: two hundred and twenty five cars and one hundred and fifty big cars

final_answer.spoken: four hundred and fifty bicycles, three hundred autorickshaws, two hundred and twenty five cars, one hundred and fifty big cars

never_show: 900 shared by 2 written before the total is found
a bigger vehicle needing more vehicles, marked as right
maths_rules: ones: 1 + 9 = 10, write 0 carry 1; tens: 6 + 3 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1; hundreds: 4 + 4 + 1 = 9; so 900
slip: a bigger vehicle needs more vehicles; the more a vehicle carries the fewer are needed (2 per bicycle gives 450, 6 per big car gives 150)
video_script.design: One idea: share the total into groups of the size one vehicle carries. Wrong idea: bigger vehicle, more vehicles. The line of vehicles stays in the anchor band; the hint card leaves at the break.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the school gate with vehicles sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a school gate with a line of empty vehicle outlines; a board shows girls 461, boys 439; four vehicle cards: bicycle 2, autorickshaw 3, car 4, big car 6

marks.m1: the small title card From your book appears
marks.m2: the school gate appears with the board girls 461, boys 439
marks.m3: a line of vehicle outlines appears at the gate
marks.m4: the bicycle card 2 and the autorickshaw card 3 appear
marks.m5: the car card 4 and the big car card 6 appear

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Joseph's school in Kochi has four hundred and sixty one girls and four hundred and thirty nine boys.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>All of them are going on a trip.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Use bicycles that carry two, and autorickshaws that carry three.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Then use cars that carry four, and big cars that carry six.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>How many vehicles are needed in each case?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.m7: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m7'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a hint card in the working band: find the total first; then equal groups, one group for each vehicle

marks.m8: the words find the total light up
marks.m9: the words equal groups light up

narration: <bookmark mark='m8'/>First find how many children are going in all.
<bookmark mark='m9'/>Then think of equal groups, with one group for each vehicle.
<bookmark mark='m10'/>Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows big car, bigger, so more vehicles; a bicycle and a big car are shown with their riders; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.m11: Chintu's bubble appears: big car, bigger, so more vehicles
marks.m12: a long line of bicycles appears, two children on each
marks.m13: a short line of big cars appears, six children in each
marks.m14: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m11'/>A big car is bigger, so it needs more vehicles than a bicycle.
<bookmark mark='m12'/>Think of bicycles. Each one carries only two children, so we need very many.
<bookmark mark='m13'/>A big car carries six, so we need fewer of them.
<bookmark mark='m14'/>The more a vehicle carries, the fewer vehicles we need.

beats.on_screen: the board adds 461 and 439 in columns with the carries marked; the total 900 glows

marks.m15: the addition 461 + 439 is set out in columns
marks.m16: the ones column shows 0 with a carry of 1
marks.m17: the tens column shows 0 with a carry of 1
marks.m18: the hundreds column shows 9 and the total 900 glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m15'/>First add the girls and the boys: four hundred and sixty one and four hundred and thirty nine.
<bookmark mark='m16'/>The ones make ten, so write zero and carry one.
<bookmark mark='m17'/>The tens and the carry make ten, so write zero and carry one again.
<bookmark mark='m18'/>The hundreds and the carry make nine, so there are nine hundred children.

beats.on_screen: two lines appear: 900 ÷ 2 = 450 bicycles and 900 ÷ 3 = 300 autorickshaws, each with a check

marks.m22: the line = 300 autorickshaws appears with its check

narration: <bookmark mark='m19'/>For bicycles, share nine hundred children into groups of two.
<bookmark mark='m20'/>Nine hundred divided by two is four hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='m21'/>For autorickshaws, share them into groups of three.
<bookmark mark='m22'/>Nine hundred divided by three is three hundred, and three hundred times three is nine hundred.

beats.on_screen: two lines appear: 900 ÷ 4 = 225 cars and 900 ÷ 6 = 150 big cars, each with a check; the four answers glow in a row
narration: <bookmark mark='m23'/>For cars, share them into groups of four.
<bookmark mark='m24'/>Nine hundred divided by four is two hundred and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='m25'/>Check: four times two hundred and twenty five is nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='m26'/>For big cars, nine hundred divided by six is one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='m27'/>We need four hundred and fifty bicycles and three hundred autorickshaws.
<bookmark mark='m28'/>We need two hundred and twenty five cars and one hundred and fifty big cars.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the four answers; two check lines appear: vehicles multiplied by riders gives 900; the more a vehicle carries, the fewer we need

marks.m29: the check line vehicles multiplied by riders appears
marks.m31: the line the more a vehicle carries, the fewer we need appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m29'/>To check, multiply the number of vehicles by how many each one carries.
<bookmark mark='m30'/>Every answer must give nine hundred again.
<bookmark mark='m31'/>A bigger vehicle always means fewer vehicles.
